newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Miners lead Australian stocks slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Miners lead Australian stocks slightly lower.

text.p: SPI futures 2746.0 -10.0 US 30yr cl 6.30 -0.02
10yrbond futs 93.685 +0.060 Gold NY 324.55 cl Asia 324.65
*Big miners lead stocks 0.3 pct lower as U.S. weakness overnight spills over. Volume 382.69 million, A$876.58 million value, 1,112 stocks traded, 301 steady, 432 up, 379 down.
Depressed mining stocks and overnight weakness on Wall Street took its toll on the Australian share market on Friday. Stocks ended 0.3 percent lower although advances outnumbered declines.

"The miners dragged the market down, but not by great numbers. It wasn't a bad day, bearing in mind that it's Friday and people don't like being exposed against Wall Street over the weekend," Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan said.
The All Ordinaries index ended 7.6 points down at 2,727.5, while September share price index futures fell 10 points to 2,746, an 18.5 point premium to the underlying market.
Big copper producer Broken Hill Pty Co shed 23 cents to A$18.01 while mining giant Rio Tinto fell 8.4 cents to A$20.793. Gold and nickel producer WMC came down 14.6 cents to A$7.64.
"We've had a long period of sustained weakness in metal prices and people are beginning to wonder if it's ever going to improve," Lourey said.

Most market players seemed to agree. "There is still some uncertainty about future direction," said Phillip Toop of Henderson Charlton Jones. "There has been nothing in particular today but people seem a little bit more pessimistic," he added.
The troubled gold share sector managed to gain a bit of ground despite the relatively weak bullion price.
Normandy Mining ended two cents up at A$1.57, while Lihir Gold climbed seven to A$1.98.
The banking sector also held up slightly better than the overall market, although the major banks were stable to lower.
NAB closed three cents down at A$19.51, and Westpac Banking fell 12.3 cents to A$8.62. The smaller St George Bank climbed 21 cents to end at A$8.95.
"They've got one of the best dividend yields, and it's fully franked," one dealer said of St George.

Rumours that a new Australian airline was being formed by Brian Grey, founder of the failed Compass Airlines, sent Qantas Airways 13 cents lower to A$2.92 before it recovered to end at an even A$3.00. "We have heard that he (Grey) is making presentations to institutions and is trying to raise A$100 million," one broker in Melbourne said. "There is also talk that he has the backing of a couple of Asian airlines."
Others said they doubted there was any truth behind the rumours, and that there were more fundamental reasons to stay away from the stock.

Fosters Brewing was one the most actively traded stocks, ending 1.8 cents lower at A$2.61. Volume was pulled up by a parcel of 15.84 million shares, worth a total of A$40.72 million, specialled through SBC Warburg at A$2.57 per share.
One of the day's better performers was HIH Winterthur which rose 12 cents to a record A$3.44.
"This is the time to go bottom-fishing," one dealer said about the stock, adding there was no news behind the rise.
Hills Motorway lost seven cents to A$1.98. J.B. Were has a "sell" recommendation on the stock and thinks a fair value range would be A$1.35 to A$1.66.

Over the week, the All Ordinaries gained 1.35 percent, and most dealers were optimistic about developments in the next few weeks following Wednesday's interest rate cut by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA). The RBA cut the cash rate by 50 basis points to 5.00 percent, the fifth reduction in a year.

"We still haven't seen the market appreciation of the effect on our economy of the cut in the interest rate. Provided we get a reasonable lead from Wall Street, we'll have a good week next week," said broker Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan.
In other markets, 10-year bond futures contracts hit a record 93.695 before falling back to 93.680.
Local long-end yields are at their lowest levels since the early 1970s and could fall further if next Thursday's labour force report proves weak, traders said.
The Australian dollar firmed on the week but at 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT) it was unchanged from Thursday's US$0.433/38. -----------------------(TECHNICALS)-------------------------
